title: Aviation Logistics Information Systems Advisor (LtCol to 2ndLt) and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (0602, 6002, 6004, 6602, 6604), DC AVN
raw_text:
5. MOS 6609, Aviation Logistics Information Systems Advisor (LtCol to 2ndLt)
and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (0602, 6002, 6004, 6602, 6604), DC AVN

    a. Summary. Aviation Logistics Information Systems Advisors are
assigned to selected headquarters and staffs. They possess knowledge of how
to establish, employ, and sustain Aviation specific information systems in
support of Marine Corps and Naval Aviation and are able to communicate
clearly with a non-technical audience. Their role is to integrate and
coordinate with the plans sections or operations sections of their respective
command as it pertains to Aviation Information Systems. They must identify
and clearly translate communications and Department of Defense Information
Network Operations (DODIN Ops) capabilities, limitations, and opportunities
in all phases of the planning cycle. The skill set provides headquarters
staffs with officers who, along with MOS 6694 subject matter expertise,
ensure that aviation information systems are considered in the force
deployment planning and execution process, exercise planning, pre-positioning
program development execution, and doctrine development.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

        (2) Must possess one of the following PMOSs MOS 6002, Aircraft
Maintenance Officer, MOS 6004, Aircraft Maintenance Engineer Officer, MOS
6602, Aviation Supply Officer, MOS 6604, Aviation Supply Operations Officer,
or MOS 0602, Communications Officer.

    c. Requirements. Must have minimum of 6 months of time in a table of
organization designated 6609 MOS billet.


                                           1-254                        Enclosure (1)
 1138                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



       d.   Duties

        (1) Identify and clearly translate aviation information systems
capabilities, limitations, and opportunities in all phases of the planning
cycle.

        (2) Support the development, review, and update of OPLANS/CONPLANS in
support of higher headquarters' directives.

            (3) Develop estimates of supportability and concepts of logistics
support.

        (4) Support the development and operational orders and letters of
instruction for ACE operations and exercises.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Computer and Information Systems Managers 11-3021.

            (2) Logisticians 13-1081.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Communications Officer, 0602.

            (2) Marine Air Ground Task Force Communications Planner, 0603.

            (3) Aviation Logistician, 6607.

        (4) Aviation Logistics Information Management System (ALIMS)
Specialist, 6694.




                                        1-255                         Enclosure (1)
 1139                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L

Aviation Logistics Information Systems Advisors are assigned to selected headquarters and staffs.
Teach company regulations and procedures to other pilots.

They possess knowledge of how to establish, employ, and sustain Aviation specific information systems in support of Marine Corps and Naval Aviation and are able to communicate clearly with a non-technical audience.
Maintain radio or telephone contact with adjacent control towers, terminal control units, or other area control centers to coordinate aircraft movement.
Their role is to integrate and coordinate with the plans sections or operations sections of their respective command as it pertains to Aviation Information Systems.
Identify operational requirements for new systems to inform selection of technological solutions.

They must identify and clearly translate communications and Department of Defense Information Network Operations (DODIN Ops) capabilities, limitations, and opportunities in all phases of the planning cycle.

The skill set provides headquarters staffs with officers who, along with MOS 6694 subject matter expertise, ensure that aviation information systems are considered in the force deployment planning and execution process, exercise planning, pre-positioning program development execution, and doctrine development.
Use airfield landing and navigational aids and digital data terminal communications equipment to perform duties.
d. Duties (1) Identify and clearly translate aviation information systems capabilities, limitations, and opportunities in all phases of the planning cycle.
Determine logistics support requirements, such as facility details, staffing needs, or safety or maintenance plans.
(3) Develop estimates of supportability and concepts of logistics support.
Support the development of training materials and technical manuals.
(4) Support the development and operational orders and letters of instruction for ACE operations and exercises.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
